item.title: How Antonelli 'blew everyone away' to make Formula 1 history
item.description: Twelve world titles on one podium - Max Verstappen and Lewis Hamilton hold Kimi Antonelli aloft [Getty Images] Just after Kimi Antonelli clinched his first title to become the youngest world champion in Formula 1 history, Lewis Hamilton and Max Verstappen were united in their assessment of his achievement. "Incredible," they both said. Coming from the two most successful champions on the current grid, the men who are first and third in the all-time list of F1 record-holders, it meant something. That Antonelli shared the Mexico City Grand Prix podium with these two titans meant something, too. To Antonelli, firstly, who said: "I will definitely frame the picture and put it in my house because it's just an incredible moment. And as well to see so much respect from two incredible drivers who have done the history of the sport is truly special and a moment that will live and will always be remembered." So, too, though, for its symbolism. Antonelli seems destined to join them among the list of all-time greats of the sport, judging by the scale of his achievement this year. "There are going to be others," said 1996 world champion Damon Hill, commentating for BBC Radio 5 live. "I don't see anything else other than him getting better and better. He's going to have to go through hard times as well, but no one is going to doubt his incredible talent." No one indeed. Not any more, anyway. Antonelli - the boy 'born in a garage' who became world champion Antonelli heads list of F1's youngest champions How much do you know about F1 champion Antonelli? Antonelli's first title comes at the end of only his second season in F1. When he was drafted into Mercedes last year - to replace Hamilton, no less - there were those who said he was too inexperienced. For some of last year, he looked it. There were flashes of promise, but by and large it was a shaky debut season, one that did not live up to Antonelli's billing as potentially the next generational talent. So when it became clear that Mercedes would start this season with the best car, it was his team-mate George Russell, who had comfortably beaten him in 2025, who was favourite for the championship. But that was without reckoning on the remarkable step forward Antonelli made in his development over last winter. He finished the first race on Russell's tail. He took his maiden victory in the second, the first of five consecutive wins with which he took control of the championship. Since then, he has never looked like losing it. Even when Mercedes' early season advantage was wiped out by their rivals, Antonelli was always there, always a factor. Which is more than can be said for Russell. In that sense, it is important to see his achievement in context. Had the comparative performance between Russell and Antonelli carried on as it did last year, this championship may well have had a different complexion. item.title: Antonelli becomes world champion as Verstappen wins in Mexico
item.description: Kimi Antonelli did not win the race in Mexico City - but he did not need to [Getty Images] Kimi Antonelli clinched his first world title and became the youngest champion in Formula 1 history by finishing third at the Mexico City Grand Prix. Antonelli - 20 years and 68 days old - finished the race in third, behind Red Bull's Max Verstappen and Ferrari's Lewis Hamilton. His moment of glory came on a day when tensions at Ferrari between seven-time champion Hamilton and team-mate Charles Leclerc came close to boiling over. Antonelli drove a composed race amid some hectic action involving the other front-runners in a grand prix interrupted by a red flag that led to a 25-lap sprint to the finish. The Italian, a teenager until late August, spent the closing laps watching Hamilton try to get close enough to pass Verstappen after the two had made contact at the first chicane at the restart. But Hamilton found it impossible to get his Ferrari close enough to Verstappen to try to pass and ended the day frustrated and feeling a win had slipped through his fingers as a consequence of Leclerc's aggression on the first lap. That was a secondary story on the day Antonelli made history, smashing Sebastian Vettel's previous record for being the youngest champion by three years and 66 days. Antonelli also becomes the first Italian to win the F1 title since Alberto Ascari in 1953. Antonelli had tears mixed with laughter over the radio on the slowing down lap as he proved initially incapable of talking when his team told him he was world champion. After he half-composed himself, he said: "Thank you so much. We did it. We did it." The key stories of the race were: Antonelli delivering the title with several races to go in a season he has taken by storm Tension at Ferrari after Leclerc's successful attempts to grab the lead on the first lap led to controversy and unhappiness at the team Verstappen benefiting from the internal battle to take his third win in four races. item.description: Kimi Antonelli has made history by becoming the youngest title winner in the 77th year of the Formula 1 World Championship. The Italian, at 20 years and 68 days, has beaten the record of Sebastian Vettel, who was 23 years and 134 days old when he won the first of his four drivers' championships in 2010. Antonelli, who was still a teenager until 25 August, has secured the title in his second season in the sport. We take a look at F1's other young champions and how Antonelli's achievement compares with theirs. In his second season, he became the youngest driver to achieve a pole position in China and the youngest to lead the championship at the next race in Japan. In Monaco, he became the youngest driver to complete a 'grand slam' of pole position, fastest lap, leading every lap and winning the race. All this after a rookie season in 2025 in which there were occasional highs but plenty of errors, and his final total of 150 points was less than half of the 319 accumulated by Mercedes team-mate George Russell. Sebastian Vettel Sebastian Vettel's four drivers' championships were won between 2010-13 [Getty Images] First championship: 2010 Age: 23 years and 134 days Stage of his F1 career when title was won: Third full season F1 debut: 2007 US Grand Prix (aged 19) Vettel was one of four drivers who could win the title going into the season-ending 2010 Abu Dhabi Grand Prix. The German did what he had to do by winning the grand prix and Alonso could only finish seventh, having become stuck behind the Renault of Vitaly Petrov. With Webber in eighth, Vettel won the championship by four points from Alonso. It was yet another F1 record for Vettel. He had become the youngest F1 points scorer on his debut for BMW Sauber in Indianapolis in 2007, before becoming the then youngest pole sitter and race winner at the 2008 Italian Grand Prix for Toro Rosso. item.title: 'We've got big problems' - Hamilton says Ferrari need 'serious talks'
item.description: Lewis Hamilton had to settle for third after securing his first pole position with Ferrari in Mexico [Getty Images] Lewis Hamilton says Ferrari "have to have some serious talks behind closed doors" after fighting between their two drivers cost them victory in the Mexico City Grand Prix. Leclerc cut a chicane on the first lap to take the lead from Hamilton, who then lost second place to Max Verstappen as a consequence of his team-mate's attack. Verstappen went on to win the race with Hamilton second, as Kimi Antonelli finished third to become the youngest world champion in Formula 1 history. "Ultimately, that lost us the win today," said Hamilton. "We have to have some serious talks behind closed doors." During a red-flag period in the race caused by a crash for Valtteri Bottas' Cadillac, Hamilton had said over team radio: "We've got big problems. Big, big problems." When informed Hamilton was unhappy, Leclerc said: "I will speak with Lewis. We both didn't make the corner. I don't know if Lewis' point was for me to get P3 but having the Red Bull second I felt it was worth it to keep the position and see what happened. That's what I did. "I could be also unhappy with how much he pushed me off track out of Turn One, but it is racing. When you are fighting for a win it is the way it should be." Hamilton's point is that if the Ferraris had worked together on the first lap, they would have been running one-two and could have controlled the race from there and likely finished in those positions. He said: "We could have easily had a one-two today. We had the pace to do so. "We're going into Turn Four first and second. If we just held position, I think anything can happen in the race. But when your team-mate works against you and then you lose positions like that, it's definitely tough. "So we'll just talk about it offline and it's not really worth saying too much more. We don't have rules of engagement. And whether or not that would change anything from Charles' side, I don't know. We've just got to figure out. But something needs to change for sure." item.title: Cole Young wins first AL Gold Glove award, first Mariners player since Raleigh, Moore in 2024
item.description: SEATTLE, WASHINGTON - APRIL 01: Cole Young #2 of the Seattle Mariners at bat during the ninth inning against the New York Yankees at T-Mobile Park on April 01, 2026 in Seattle, Washington. (Photo by Steph Chambers/Getty Images) Steph Chambers It’s official -- Cole Young is a 2026 American League Gold Glove winner. This is the first Gold Glove award of Cole Young’s career. Young is the first Mariners player to win a Gold Glove award since both Cal Raleigh and Dylan Moore won back in 2024. In addition, Young is the third second baseman in Mariners history to win a Gold Glove award, after Bret Boone and Harold Reynolds, according to the Mariners. Despite a rather tough overall 2025-2026 campaign, Young was a standout on the Mariners , tallying 16 runs saved and over 220 putouts. Young also had a fielding percentage of .990 and “lead the American League second basemen in nearly every traditional defensive category,” according to the Mariners.

item.title: Jerry Koosman, 1969 World Series Champ Who Is in ‘One of the Most Iconic Images’ in MLB History, Dies at 83
item.description: Jerry Koosman, who played for the New York Mets from 1967 to 1978; Koosman (middle) celebrates winning the World Series with Ed Charles (left) and Jerry Grote (right) on Oct. 16, 1969 Credit: Ron Vesely/Getty NEED TO KNOW Jerry Koosman died at age 83 in Osceola, Wis., on Nov. 1 The former New York Mets pitcher, a father of three, died “after battling multiple illnesses,” team historian Jay Horwitz said Koosman is known for clinching the World Series title in 1969 Jerry Koosman, the MLB pitcher who was an integral part of the “Miracle Mets” winning the World Series in 1969, has died. He was 83. Koosman, a father of three, died “after battling multiple illnesses” in Osceola, Wis., on Sunday, Nov. 1, the New York Mets announced on X . “The 1969 Mets had a multitude of heroes, but no one was bigger than Jerry Koosman, who passed away this morning after battling multiple illnesses,” team historian Jay Horwitz wrote in a tribute on Medium , adding that the MLB alum died “surrounded by his family.” Jerry Koosman in 1969; Koosman when the Mets retired his jersey number in 2021 Credit: Mike Stobe/Getty; Sporting News via Getty Images via Getty Follow your favorite athletes on and off the field with PEOPLE’s free sports newsletter — sign up now! Horwitz recalled Koosman’s pivotal role in the Mets’ championship win in ’69, saying, “After the Mets lost game 1 of the World Series, Jerry won game 2 and also the clinching game 5.” The MLB elaborated on that game-winning moment in a tribute on X . “On Oct. 16, 1969, in Game 5 of the World Series, Koosman threw a complete-game five-hitter against Baltimore for his second win of the series, this one clinching the world championship for the ‘Miracle Mets.’ The image of Koosman leaping into catcher Jerry Grote’s arms after the final out remains one of the most iconic images in baseball history,” the league wrote. Jerry Koosman jumps into Jerry Grote’s arms as they celebrate winning the World Series alongside Ed Charles on Oct. 16, 1969 Credit: Getty Koosman spent his first 12 seasons with the Mets before playing for the Twins, White Sox and Phillies — winning 222 games in his 19-year career. In announcing his death, the New York Mets wrote, “We are saddened to share the news that Jerry Koosman has passed away. We send our thoughts and prayers to his family.” The Mets retired Koosman’s jersey — No. 36 — in 2021. Read the original article on People

item.title: Tigers catcher Dillon Dingler wins second straight Gold Glove Award
item.description: DETROIT — Move over Pudge Rodriguez and Lance Parrish, move over Bill Freehan. Make some space among the top tier of Tigers catchers for Dillon Dingler. Dingler, just like his predecessors, has won consecutive Gold Glove awards. Rawlings announced the winners Sunday night, Nov. 2, and Dingler beat out the Yankees’ Austin Wells and the Blue Jays’ Brandon Valenzuela for American League honors in a vote of managers and coaches. Dingler, in his age-27 season, led baseball with 15 defensive runs saved. His plus-17 catcher runs (per Statcast) ranked in the top 99th percentile in baseball. He ranked in the 100th percentile in framing (plus-9), 95th percentile in blocking (plus-11) and pop time (1.86 sconds) and 93rd percentile in caught stealing (plus-5). He also expertly shepherded an ever-changing pitching staff through a tumultuous season, which earned praise from Tigers’ president Scott Harris. “There’s a whole subset of his game that is really valuable, but not necessarily measurable,” Harris said. “Like his impact on our pitching staff, his impact on game-calling, his preparation going into every game, the effect that he has on pitchers in really tough times to get them out of a game.” Dingler also posted a career-high 145 times, starting 116 times behind the plate and 29 times serving as the designated hitter. Offensively, he clubbed 27 homers and drove in 91 runs, despite his production declining in the second half of the season. “I continued to play him because I trust him to come out of it,” manager AJ Hinch said. “He’s going to be able to learn to maybe audible the swing or change a little bit of his prep routine. Or maybe it’s just going to be mentally how he balances offense and defense. But I’m not disappointed in the least bit that he had to go through the tough time. “I felt for him. I was not going to let off the gas pedal because we needed him and his presence in the lineup, and he didn’t complain a bit.” Zach McKinstry was a finalist for multi-position Gold Glove award. He played six different positions and ranked in the top 95th percentile with a plus-12 fielding run value. He ranked third in baseball among right fielders with 13 defensive runs saved. He was third among America League right fielders with nine outfield assists. Both Dingler and McKinstry also won Fielding Bible Awards, presented by Sports Info Solutions. item.title: ‘It’s like he’s trying to lose’: Donald Trump sparks reactions after calling football ‘boring’
item.description: President Donald Trump speaks during a rally at the Choctaw Event Center in Durant, Okla., on Thursday, Oct. 1, 2026. Football is one of the most popular things in America, especially in the Midwest amongst blue-collar voters. So it might not have been the wisest move for President Donald Trump to trash the sport two days before the midterm elections. At a campaign rally in Iowa on Sunday, Trump questioned why anyone would want to watch football, calling it “boring as hell.” Many were quick to point out that it might not be the best closing message for Republicans. ‘Who the Hell Wants to Watch Football?’ Trump was in Iowa to campaign for Senate candidate Ashley Hinson ahead of Tuesday’s elections. But he once again went on a tangent about the NFL’s dynamic kickoff rule, which he has complained about repeatedly since it was introduced in 2024. “Well, who the hell wants to watch football? It’s boring as hell. And I hate, I hate that new kickoff rule where you hit the ball and the people are standing there like a bunch of idiots,” Trump said in a clip shared by Aaron Rupar . Trump said that he can’t even bring himself to watch the start of games anymore. “You know what I do? I start the game about 2 minutes in. I don’t want to watch the kickoff. I think it’s so disparaging,” Trump said. “They have no right to ruin football by doing [stuff] like that.” ‘Trying to Lose’ Needless to say, Trump’s comments led to a lot of reactions on social media. “Two days before the midterms, Trump goes on stage and trashes football: ‘Who the hell wants to watch football? It’s boring as hell.’ Bold closing message for the heartland,” wrote Ed Krassenstein , a progressive political commentator. “It’s like he’s trying to lose,” wrote Jack Cocchiarella , a progressive political YouTuber. “This man has to be trying to lose at this point,” wrote Jared Shult , a progressive TikTok creator. “Brilliant strategy for the Republicans to make the midterms all about this buffoon instead of just letting individual candidates run their races,” wrote Ron Filipkowski , editor-in-chief of MeidasTouch. “Republicans just lost Michigan, Ohio, Georgia, Florida, and Texas lol,” wrote Zaid Jilani , author of the newsletter The American Saga . “The idiot doesn’t even know how much MAGA loves football. Hell of a closing argument!” wrote Morgan J. Former New York Rangers First-Round Bust Waived According to Sportsnet’s Elliotte Friedman , former Rangers defenseman Dylan McIlrath has been placed on waivers by the Washington Capitals. The Capitals waiving McIlrath comes just a few hours after they acquired goalie Remi Poirier from the New Jersey Devils. However, if he passes through them unclaimed, Washington will then be able to assign him to their AHL affiliate, the Hershey Bears . Looking Back at McIlrath’s Time With the Rangers The Rangers selected McIlrath in the first round of the 2010 NHL Entry Draft, 10th overall. The expectation was that he would blossom into a star shutdown defenseman for them. However, that ended up being far from the case. McIlrath had trouble cementing himself as an NHL-caliber defenseman while the Rangers. He appeared in just 38 games over four seasons with the Rangers from 2013-14 to 2016-17. During them, he posted two goals, four points, 84 penalty minutes, and 99 hits. McIlrath’s time with New York ended during the 2016-17 season when he was traded to the Florida Panthers for Steven Kampfer and a 2018 seventh-round pick. item.description: Photo by: Mark Konezny The Buffalo Bills delivered an impressive second half performance Sunday, defeating the Baltimore Ravens 36-10 at Highmark Stadium. Josh Allen led the way with three total touchdowns as Buffalo improved to 6-1, while Baltimore suffered another disappointing loss and lost quarterback Lamar Jackson to a serious thumb injury. The game started with plenty of excitement, as Allen opened the scoring with a one-yard rushing touchdown. Buffalo added a 56 yard field goal from Tyler Bass to take an early 10-0 lead. However, Baltimore responded after Jackson left the game with a right thumb injury on his first offensive snap. Derrick Henry scored on a two yard touchdown run, bringing the Ravens back within three points. Josh Allen Takes Control Buffalo entered halftime with a 16-7 advantage, but the offense found another gear after the break. James Cook extended the lead with a five yard rushing touchdown before Allen connected with D.J. Moore for an 11-yard score. Allen added another touchdown pass late in the game, finding Dalton Kincaid for a 23-yard score that put the contest out of reach. The Bills quarterback finished with 289 passing yards, two passing touchdowns, one interception and a rushing touchdown. His touchdown pass to Moore also moved him past Jim Kelly for the most passing touchdowns in Bills franchise history. Ravens Lose Two Quarterbacks Baltimore’s afternoon became even worse when backup Tyler Huntley also exited with a toe injury. That forced undrafted rookie Joe Fagnano into his NFL debut. Fagnano finished with 91 passing yards, one interception and a lost fumble as Buffalo’s defense continued applying pressure. The Ravens managed only 144 total yards, while Henry provided their lone touchdown. Buffalo Sends a Message The 36-10 victory gives Buffalo its third consecutive win and keeps the Bills near the top of the AFC. Baltimore, meanwhile, has lost three straight games and faces serious questions at quarterback heading into its Thursday matchup against Jacksonville. The Bills made a statement with a dominant second-half performance, but the biggest story of the afternoon was Jackson’s injury and what it could mean for Baltimore’s season.

item.title: Shane van Gisbergen charges from 29th to fifth at Martinsville
item.description: Motorsport photo Shane van Gisbergen missed the Chase, but he continues to make gains on the ovals, earning a top-five finish at Martinsville Speedway. Van Gisbergen started 29th and didn't make it to the top ten until the final stage of the race, but he made much of his progress during the long green-flag runs. He was the only driver who started outside the top 20 to finish inside the top 10, and was set to battle teammate Ross Chastain for that top five before a pit stop error knocked Chastain down the order. That left Van Gisbergen as Trackhouse's highest finisher, placing fifth for his third-ever oval top five in the Cup Series. He also finished fifth at Nashville and North Wilkesboro earlier this year, and his previous best result at Martinsville was a 12th as a part-time driver in 2024. "I guess the Wendy's car is good luck," said Van Gisbergen with a smile. "We got another top five with it, so pretty stoked with that. Just an awesome day. Pissed at myself (for) yesterday qualifying. If we started up front, maybe we would have had a better shot. Thanks to my Trackhouse team all day. We just methodically worked forward. Got in a couple little incidents, fixed it up, and got a good result." He later added in a separate interview: “I definitely feel like I’m getting there, thanks to having a great team around me ... The first stage was awesome with the different strategies. We managed to stay on the lead lap and we just kept working forward. I enjoyed it.” Van Gisbergen remains the highest-ranked driver outside the Chase field, holding 17th in the standings with a 29-point advantage over teammate Chastain entering the Homestead finale. item.description: Steve Roberts-Imagn Images NFL rumors: Titans’ AFC South rival called about Jeffery Simmons trade before Bears blockbuster appeared first on ClutchPoints . The Chicago Bears ’ blockbuster trade for Jeffery Simmons have made them immediate Super Bowl contenders, combining him with Grady Jarrett to create one of the league’s most formidable interior defensive line combinations. However, the Tennessee Titans , as one would expect, received calls from multiple other teams inquiring the availability of the 29-year-old defensive tackle. Among them was division rivals Jacksonville Jaguars, according to The Ringer’s Tom Pelissero. “While trading a core player within the AFC South was probably a nonstarter, it’s a reminder that GM James Gladstone is willing to be aggressive in any area that potentially can improve the team, and probably portends more activity in Jacksonville over the next 10 days,” Pelissero noted. Simmons was acquired in exchange for 2027 and 2028 first-round picks and a 2027 fourth-round selection, along with a 2028 fifth-round pick. As a result, he became the first defensive tackle in the common draft era to be traded for multiple first-round selections. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) The 29-year-old arrives after spending his entire NFL career in Tennessee, who selected him 19th overall in 2019, and brings 46.5 sacks, 72 tackles for loss and 96 quarterback hits across eight seasons. He was named a first-team All-Pro for the first time in 2025 after recording a career-high 11 sacks, and continued producing in a difficult season for the Titans. Chicago’s need for interior disruption was a major factor in the move as the Bears ranked 23rd in interior defensive pass-rush win rate at 13%, while Simmons led the NFL’s defensive tackles with a 27% win rate. Simmons will join a defensive front featuring Grady Jarrett and Montez Sweat, who is returning from a two-game suspension, and the move follows their earlier additions of safety Coby Bryant and linebacker Devin Bush.
